assessments.assessment: Classical ideal gas in thermal equilibrium, without bulk flow relative to the container. Stationary, smooth, very massive walls are explicitly an approximation; elastic collisions preserve molecular kinetic energy in this model. Real wall energy exchange is not falsely excluded universally.

Pre-collision subscript-zero and post-collision components are distinguished. Reversing the normal component gives molecular signed momentum change 2mv_x, while wall collision impulse is opposite and has magnitude 2m|v_x|. Smoothness, not elasticity alone, justifies unchanged tangential components. Original vector/component expressions and(3-6) retained.

assessments.topic: Toy collision-count model and time interval
assessments.assessment: Equal normal-speed magnitudes with both directions are explicitly a toy distribution. Incoming v_x>0 is locally identified as pre-impact motion toward the right wall, not the negative post-impact component used earlier. Short-time, many-particle, rare-intermolecular-collision assumptions are probabilistic rather than a claim of no collisions. Half toward the wall is a statistical mean, not an exact finite-sample split.

assessments.topic: Number density, geometry and side-wall motion
assessments.assessment: n is explicitly number per unit volume, distinguished from prior n31's total molecule count. The source thin-layer volume, collision count and side-wall argument remain correct under the stated smooth-wall/short-time model. No source geometry is presented as a measured quantity.

assessments.topic: Mean force and real velocity distribution
assessments.assessment: Force in(3-8) is time-averaged collision force, not an individual impact peak. Independently summing collision flux times per-impact impulse over symmetric velocity classes yields mnS times the all-molecule mean of v_x squared, multiplied by the interval. Faster normal motion contributes both more hits and larger impulses; the averaging step is not replaced by mean velocity squared.

The one-third factor requires isotropic second moments in the container rest frame, not merely three coordinate directions or many collisions. Removing time and area yields p=(1/3)mn times mean speed squared. Equilibrium/no-directed-drive qualifications and the real-gas ideal approximation are retained. Mean square is correctly distinguished from root-mean-square speed and bulk flow.

Independent dimensional checks: Z is dimensionless, force times time has momentum units, mn times mean speed squared has pressure units. Mean translational energy equals half the molecular mass times mean speed squared, giving p=(2/3)n times that energy. Internal rotation/vibration, intermolecular potential and bulk-flow energy are not conflated with random center-of-mass translation. No numerical measurements or unsupported temperature formula added.
